questions.html:
$A, B$ and $C$ are arbitrary, non-singular matrices. $\operatorname{det}\left(A^{T} B\right)$ must equal which of the following?
    A. $\operatorname{det}(A) \operatorname{det}(B)$
    
    B. $\dfrac{\operatorname{det}(B)}{\operatorname{det}(A)}$
    
    C. $\operatorname{det}\left(A^{-1}\right) \operatorname{det}(B)$
    
    D. $\dfrac{\operatorname{det}(B)}{\operatorname{det}\left(A^{-1}\right)}$
questions.solution:

Suppose $A$ is $3$ by $4,$ and $A x=0$ has all solutions in the following form -
$$
\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{s}\left[\begin{array}{l}
1 \\
1 \\
1 \\
0
\end{array}\right]+\mathrm{t}\left[\begin{array}{r}
-2 \\
-1 \\
0 \\
1
\end{array}\right]

We do some unknown elementary row transformations on $A$ and get the following matrix $R$ -
$$
R=\left[\begin{array}{llll}
1 & 0 & \mathrm{a} & \mathrm{b} \\
0 & 1 & \mathrm{c} & \mathrm{d} \\
0 & 0 & 0 & 0
\end{array}\right]
$$
What will be the values of $a, b, c,$ and $d?$

   D. $d=1$

    B. Suppose $A x=b$ has the solution, the solution unique solution if and only if $A x=0$ has unique solution.
    
    C. If $A$ is an $m \times n$ matrix and $A x=0$ has a unique solution, then $A x=b$ is consistent for every $b$ in $\mathbf{R}^{m}$.
    
    D. If for some matrix $A$, and some vectors $x$ and $b$, we have $A x=b$, then $b$ is linear combination of columns of $A$.
